expected_relationships.proposition: The entry point validates input and delegates bounded plan construction to the planner.
The entry point sends the frozen plan through the broker rather than dispatching directly.
The broker records durable intent before dispatch and seals a result digest after dispatch.
Recovery distinguishes pending intent from a sealed terminal result and prohibits automatic replay of indeterminate dispatch.
The planner propagates the registered maximum-child limit of four into each frozen plan.
The recovery test exercises the no-replay behavior described by the recovery implementation.
The network-denial test supports the broker-only request boundary in the broker implementation.
Commit a91 introduced intent-before-dispatch behavior and corresponding recovery coverage.
Commit b07 introduced indeterminate classification and no automatic replay in recovery.
Commit c42 hardened broker-only child requests and direct-network denial.
The release groups three chronological hardening changes covering intent, recovery, and brokered networking.
The frozen tree contains every code, configuration, test, and history surface referenced by the 0.4 hardening release analysis.
